event.name: 24 May 2009 Lake Doirani earthquake (Greece-North Macedonia border)
event.tectonic_setting: Western margin of the Serbo-Macedonian massif near Lake Doirani; N-S extension, northern Greece–North Macedonia border region

reference.title: The 24 May 2009 Mw5.2 earthquake sequence near Lake Doirani (FYROM-Greek borders): Focal mechanisms and slip model using empirical source time functions inversion

inversion.method: Finite-fault inversion of normalized empirical source time functions (STFs) from 13 regional broadband stations; source time functions obtained by deconvolution of Mw 4.4 aftershock records and stacking three components, using a radially expanding rupture front and fixed-duration boxcar subfault contributions. Best-fit rupture velocity 2.7 km/s and rise time 1.0 s, approximately 95% variance reduction.
inversion.green_function_model: Empirical Green’s functions (eGF) using the Mw 4.4 earthquake at 2009-05-24 16:23:09.8 UTC, with a half-space ray approximation for differential timing; regional synthetic waveform/moment tensor calculations used Saikia (1994) synthetics and Novotný et al. (2001) Earth model.
inversion.notes: FIGURE-DIGITIZED SLIP, NOT ORIGINAL NUMERICAL INVERSION VALUES. Sampled 15 × 20 centers (1 km × 1 km) from published Figure 8, matching NL×Nw=15×20 and its 0–15 cm slip scale. RGB samples are calibrated against each 1-cm color-band center of the published colorbar and summarized per image cell after excluding dark grid lines, contour lines and white hypocenter star. Values are discretized to 0.5-cm color-band midpoints, so do not imply 0.5-cm instrumental precision; expected reading error is often at least ±1–2 cm where contours cross cell centers, and peak values may be missed by coarse center sampling. The figure is a smoothed contour map, not an image of original inversion mesh values. The published local maximum is 15 cm, average over ruptured area 3 cm and compact slipped area ~6 × 8 km; reconstructed cell maximum and grid-cell mean are not those published statistics. Baseline red represents the bottom slip class (<~1 cm) and has been coded as 0 cm. One uncolored top row (0–1 km down dip) and one uncolored left column (0–1 km along strike), visible in Figure 8, are coded as zero for a complete 15×20 numeric grid; this is a missing-color convention, not proof of exactly zero slip there. The paper shows ONE hypocenter star, NOT aftershocks superposed on this slip figure. Do not treat the white star, black numerical labels, contours or grid as slip. Table 1 reports preferred north-dipping nodal plane with 281/59/-67 degrees; the text rounds it to 282/60 degrees. x increases ESE to WNW, y increases in down-dip distance although Figure 8 labels values 0 to −20 km. Hypocenter star is at approximately x=7.5 km and down-dip=12 km, with independently tabulated hypocentral depth 7 km. Relative depth in patch centers is approximated by 7+(down_dip_km−12)×sin(59°) and is NULL when this formula gives unphysical negative depth in empty model-border cells; plot ordinate is NOT itself an absolute depth. Since the figure provides no georeferenced corner of the plane, lat/lon of individual patches are NULL, and reference_point below is only the hypocenter for map context rather than a true plane corner. A 15×20 km plotted plane is not equivalent to a 15×20 km ruptured area. No claim is made that reconstructed slip integrates to the published moment. Original detailed faulting_style description: normal faulting with oblique-slip component. Digitization variant descriptor: figure8_colorbar_calibrated_center_sampling.
